**Report 23‑00116‑148 – Comprehensive Healthcare Inspection of the Boise VA Medical Center (Idaho)**  
*Published 2024‑04‑16* – <https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-program/comprehensive-healthcare-inspection-boise-va-0>  
*Data as of 2026‑11‑04*  

**Scope & Focus**  
The OIG performed a focused evaluation of care delivered at the Boise VA Medical Center and its outpatient clinics in Idaho and Oregon. The inspection examined five operational areas:

1. Leadership and organizational risks  
2. Quality, safety, and value  
3. Medical‑staff privileging  
4. Environment of care  
5. Mental health – suicide‑prevention initiatives  

**Key Findings & Recommendations**  
Four recommendations were issued, all of which have been closed as implemented.

| # | Domain | Finding (summarized) | OIG Recommendation (as quoted) | VA Response & Target Date |
|---|--------|----------------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Environment of Care – Panic‑alarm testing** | Inpatient Psychiatry Unit panic‑alarm response times were not consistently documented. | *“The Medical Center Director and the facility Chief, Police Service evaluated the finding…implemented a new process to document VA Police response times on an Inpatient Psychiatry Unit panic alarm response time tracking log. …Monthly auditing will monitor compliance…Goal ≥ 90 % for six consecutive months; results reported to the Quality and Safety Council.”* | Closed‑implemented 9 Oct 2024; target 31 Oct 2024. |
| 2 | **Environment of Care – Over‑the‑door alarm maintenance** | Monthly preventive‑maintenance work orders for over‑the‑door alarms on patient‑room corridor doors were missing. | *“The Biomedical Engineer updated the electronic preventive‑maintenance system to generate monthly work orders for these alarms. Auditing will monitor compliance ≥ 90 % for six consecutive months; results reported to the Quality and Safety Council.”* | Closed‑implemented 28 Oct 2024; target 31 Oct 2024. |
| 3 | **Mental‑Health / Suicide Prevention – Event reporting** | Suicide‑related events were not consistently reported to mental‑health leadership and quality‑management staff. | *“The Suicide Prevention Coordinator now reports suicide‑related event data monthly to the Quality and Safety Council and emails the data to Behavioral‑Health Leadership. Two audits (Council reporting & email distribution) will monitor ≥ 90 % compliance for six months; results reported quarterly.”* | Closed‑implemented 30 Sep 2024; target 31 Oct 2024. |
| 4 | **Mental‑Health / Suicide Prevention – Comprehensive risk evaluation** | After a positive Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale screen, staff sometimes failed to complete the required Comprehensive Suicide Risk Evaluation note. | *“Single‑point lesson documents and face‑to‑face/self‑directed training were provided (June–Aug 2023). Starting Apr 2024 a pop‑up notification and daily compliance monitoring will track completion. Goal ≥ 90 % compliance, sustained for two quarters; quarterly reporting to the Quality and Safety Council.”* | Closed‑implemented 28 Oct 2024; target 31 Dec 2024. |

**Overall Assessment**  
The inspection concluded that the Boise VA Medical Center had notable gaps in **environment‑of‑care alarm testing/maintenance** and **suicide‑prevention processes**. The VA implemented corrective actions, established auditing and reporting mechanisms, and set compliance targets (≥ 90 % sustained over multiple months). All four recommendations were closed as implemented by late 2024.

**Standards Cited**  
The report references numerous statutes, VHA directives, handbooks, and Joint Commission standards (e.g., VHA Directive 1190, 1004.08, 1100.16, Joint Commission PI.03.01.01, etc.) that underpin the required alarm‑testing, preventive‑maintenance, and suicide‑prevention practices.

**Bottom line**  
The Boise VA Medical Center addressed the OIG‑identified deficiencies through updated policies, staff training, automated work‑order generation, and systematic audit/reporting processes. The corrective actions are documented as completed and are being monitored to ensure sustained compliance.
